jobs.description:
***APPLY BY: Until Filled***

Are you a senior rotary-wing aviation professional ready to lead the helicopter side of one of the most significant aerial firefighting programs in the country, at a moment when CAL FIRE is actively modernizing its rotary-wing fleet with the Sikorsky S-70i Firehawk?

As Rotary-Wing Pilot Program Manager with CAL FIRE, you'll step into a senior aviation program leadership role at the top of CAL FIRE's helicopter operations. This position is built for an experienced aviation professional who understands rotary-wing operations, helicopter pilot training and qualification, and program leadership at a senior level, and who's ready to lead the pilot program behind one of the largest state-run rotary-wing aerial firefighting operations in the country.

This role is ideal for a senior aviation leader who can balance technical rotary-wing expertise with program management, pilot development, and operational partnership. You'll oversee the rotary-wing pilot program across CAL FIRE aviation, guide pilot training and qualification standards for the Firehawk and Huey fleets, coordinate helicopter crew certification and currency requirements, support rotary-wing operations doctrine and standards development, contribute to fleet modernization strategy as CAL FIRE continues the transition from the legacy Huey fleet to the Firehawk, and serve as the senior rotary-wing voice in how the program evolves.

This position is located at McClellan Airport in Sacramento County and is a permanent, full-time senior aviation program leadership role. This is an "Until Filled" recruitment, which means applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis without an artificial closing date. Expect the operational tempo of a busy fire aviation program during California's fire seasons, with the strategic responsibility that comes with leading a rotary-wing program in the middle of a historic fleet transition.

This isn't a general aviation management role. Rotary-wing program leadership at CAL FIRE right now sits at the intersection of legacy operations, active modernization, and mission-critical aerial firefighting delivery. This is a chance to lead that work at a rank and scope where openings are genuinely rare.

Why CAL FIRE?

State benefits including health, dental, vision, and retirement
Permanent, full-time senior aviation program leadership career opportunity
Statewide rotary-wing program leadership in one of the largest state-run helicopter aerial firefighting operations in the country
Direct leadership during CAL FIRE's Firehawk fleet modernization, one of the most significant fire aviation transitions in the country
Rare senior aviation program leadership opening at the state level
Mission driven team culture focused on service, readiness, and the pilots and aircrews who protect California from the air

About Sacramento County and McClellan Airport

Sacramento County is home to CAL FIRE's Aviation Management Program at McClellan Airport, one of the most recognizable fire aviation bases in the country. The location gives senior aviation professionals a strong mix of urban convenience, aviation community, and proximity to some of California's best outdoor escapes.

With a lower cost of living than the Bay Area or Southern California, easy access to Lake Tahoe, the Sierra Nevada, the Northern California coast, and the wine regions of Napa and Sonoma, Sacramento County is a strong fit for senior aviation program leaders who want mission-critical work and a quality of life that isn't dominated by commute time.

jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference
. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Job Summary

Etched is seeking a highly skilled and motivated ASIC Technical Program Manager to join our silicon team. This is a hands-on, high-accountability role for someone who has lived inside the ASIC development cycle and can drive technical execution, not just track it. You will own program coordination across Physical Design, DFT, DV, and RTL teams while managing relationships with external vendors including IP providers, implementation partners, and EDA tool vendors. The ideal candidate has real tape-out experience, understands the full RTL-to-GDSII flow, and operates with the urgency and proactivity that a first-silicon program demands.

Key Responsibilities

Cross-Functional Technical Coordination: Own program management across Physical Design, DFT, DV, RTL, and Post-Silicon teams. Understand inter-team dependencies - know who owns what, when handoffs need to happen, and what needs to be signed off before downstream work can begin (e.g., RTL version gates for synthesis, DFT insertion checkpoints, ECO cycles).
Vendor Management: Engage directly with external vendors, including EDA partners and implementation partners. Hold vendors accountable to timelines and deliverables. Be prepared to push back, defend Etched’s technical requirements, and escalate when needed.
Risk Identification and Mitigation: Proactively surface critical path risks, schedule slippage, and cross-team blockers. Develop mitigation strategies in partnership with engineering leads and escalate appropriately to technical and executive stakeholders.
Project Planning and Execution: Manage the scheduling and execution of complex, multi-team hardware programs. Keep projects on track across tape-out milestones, synthesis respins, and signoff cycles.
Stakeholder Communication: Provide regular, clear updates to engineering leads, VP-level stakeholders, and executive leadership on project status, risks, and decisions required. Set the tone for meetings, facilitate alignment, mediate technical disagreements, and drive to decisions.
Process Coordination: Work with ops and engineering teams to maintain accurate tracking of program state, action owners, and open items. Support the adoption of tooling and dashboards that improve engineering visibility - though dashboard creation itself sits with the ops team.
Technical Acumen: Bring enough ASIC domain knowledge to communicate credibly with engineers across the design stack and with external partners. You don’t need to be a designer, but you need to know the difference between a .3 and .5 RTL release, understand where DFT fits in the flow, and have a feel for what a synthesis restart actually involves.

You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)

At least one full ASIC tape-out under your belt. You should be able to speak fluently to what that process looks like end-to-end.
Solid understanding of the RTL-to-GDSII flow, including where Physical Design, DFT, DV, and RTL teams intersect and hand off to each other.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role within the semiconductor or hardware space.
Experience working directly with external EDA vendors or implementation partners - you’ve been in those rooms and know how to hold your ground.
Exceptional follow-through and proactivity. You chase down dependencies; you don’t wait for them to surface.
Strong communication and facilitation skills - you set a productive tone in meetings, keep discussions on track, and bring people to alignment.
Comfort with fast-paced, ambiguous startup environments where priorities shift and programs evolve quickly.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

Benefits

Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
$500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

Housing subsidy of $2k per month for those living within walking distance of the office
Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)
Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more
Daily lunch and dinner in our office
Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification

How We’re Different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

Support continuous improvement of Hydrosat’s program management processes, templates, and tools.

jobs.description:
Find your calling at Mercy!

A community health worker is a front-line public health worker who is a trusted member of and/or has an unusually close understanding of the community served. This trusting relationship enables the worker to serve as a liaison/link between health/social services and the community to facilitate access to services and improve the quality and cultural competence of service delivery. Performs duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with our mission, values, and Mercy Service Standards.

Position Details

Community Health Worker II

Overview

The Community Health Worker II (CHW II)
provides onsite support to patients across hospital and clinic settings, serving as a key member of an integrated healthcare team. This role focuses on identifying and addressing health-related social needs (HRSNs), improving access to healthcare services, and connecting patients with community resources that support overall well-being.

The Community Health Worker II acts as an advocate, educator, and resource navigator, helping patients overcome barriers to care and achieve improved health outcomes through individualized support and follow-up.

Key Responsibilities

Navigate the Health and Human Services System

Work one-on-one with patients who screen positive for health-related social needs.
Provide real-time support, including walk-in assistance, by addressing social needs, answering questions, and connecting patients to appropriate services and resources.
Educate and assist patients with applying for healthcare coverage and gathering required documentation.
Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to support patient needs.
Educate patients regarding Healthcare Marketplace options and enrollment.
Assist patients in applying for financial assistance and medication assistance programs.
Facilitate access to healthcare services and coordinate referrals as needed.
Conduct follow-up to ensure patients have successfully accessed services, attended appointments, and resolved barriers to care.

Connect Patients to Community Resources

Ensure health-related social needs screenings are completed and documented.
Connect patients with community resources through established referral processes.
Develop and maintain relationships with community-based organizations and service providers.
Promote awareness of available resources to support patient success.

Documentation and Reporting

Document patient interactions, referrals, and interventions accurately within the electronic medical record (EMR).
Maintain required records and track patient encounters according to organizational guidelines.
Prepare reports and documentation as requested.

Professional Development

Participate in Community Health Worker training programs and continuing education opportunities.
Maintain required certifications and actively engage in professional growth activities.

Caseload Management

Manage an assigned patient caseload and prioritize patient needs effectively.
Conduct outreach and follow-up via telephone, MyMercy messages, and other approved communication tools.
Monitor patient progress and identify opportunities for additional support.

Additional Duties

Perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Education

High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Experience

1-3 years of Community Health Worker experience or equivalent experience required.

Certification/Registration

Community Health Worker Training Certification (provided by Mercy) within 6-12 months of hire.
Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required.

Skills & Knowledge

Strong interpersonal, relationship-building, and collaboration skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication abilities.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
Compassion for underserved and vulnerable populations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
Reliable transportation required.

Preferred Qualifications

Skills & Knowledge

Bilingual or multilingual language skills relevant to the community served.
Experience navigating healthcare, social service, or community resource systems.

Why Join Us?

As a Community Health Worker II, you will play a vital role in improving access to care and helping patients navigate the healthcare system. Through compassionate advocacy, resource coordination, and patient support, you will make a meaningful impact on the health and well-being of the communities we serve.

Why Mercy?

From day one, Mercy offers outstanding benefits - including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, tuition support, and matched retirement plans for team members working 32+ hours per pay period.

Join a caring, collaborative team where your voice matters. At Mercy, you'll help shape the future of healthcare through innovation, technology, and compassion. As we grow, you'll grow with us.

Cross-Functional Technical Coordination: Own program management across Physical Design, DFT, DV, RTL, and Post-Silicon teams. Vendor Management: Engage directly with external vendors, including EDA partners and implementation partners. Hold vendors accountable to timelines and deliverables. Be prepared to push back, defend Etched’s technical requirements, and escalate when needed.
Risk Identification and Mitigation: Proactively surface critical path risks, schedule slippage, and cross-team blockers. Develop mitigation strategies in partnership with engineering leads and escalate appropriately to technical and executive stakeholders.
Project Planning and Execution: Manage the scheduling and execution of complex, multi-team hardware programs. Keep projects on track across tape-out milestones, synthesis respins, and signoff cycles.
Stakeholder Communication: Provide regular, clear updates to engineering leads, VP-level stakeholders, and executive leadership on project status, risks, and decisions required. Set the tone for meetings, facilitate alignment, mediate technical disagreements, and drive to decisions.
Process Coordination: Work with ops and engineering teams to maintain accurate tracking of program state, action owners, and open items. Support the adoption of tooling and dashboards that improve engineering visibility - though dashboard creation itself sits with the ops team.
Technical Acumen: Bring enough ASIC domain knowledge to communicate credibly with engineers across the design stack and with external partners. You don’t need to be a designer, but you need to know the difference between a .3 and .5 RTL release, understand where DFT fits in the flow, and have a feel for what a synthesis restart actually involves.

At least one full ASIC tape-out under your belt. You should be able to speak fluently to what that process looks like end-to-end.
Solid understanding of the RTL-to-GDSII flow, including where Physical Design, DFT, DV, and RTL teams intersect and hand off to each other.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role within the semiconductor or hardware space.
Experience working directly with external EDA vendors or implementation partners - you’ve been in those rooms and know how to hold your ground.
Exceptional follow-through and proactivity. You chase down dependencies; you don’t wait for them to surface.
Strong communication and facilitation skills - you set a productive tone in meetings, keep discussions on track, and bring people to alignment.
Comfort with fast-paced, ambiguous startup environments where priorities shift and programs evolve quickly.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
$500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

A community health worker is a front-line public health worker who is a trusted member of and/or has an unusually close understanding of the community served. Position Details

Overview

Develop and maintain relationships with community-based organizations and service providers.
Promote awareness of available resources to support patient success.

Prepare reports and documentation as requested.

Caseload Management

Conduct outreach and follow-up via telephone, MyMercy messages, and other approved communication tools.
Monitor patient progress and identify opportunities for additional support.

Perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Education

Experience

Community Health Worker Training Certification (provided by Mercy) within 6-12 months of hire.
Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required.

Strong interpersonal, relationship-building, and collaboration skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication abilities.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
Compassion for underserved and vulnerable populations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
Reliable transportation required.

Preferred Qualifications

Skills & Knowledge

Bilingual or multilingual language skills relevant to the community served.
Experience navigating healthcare, social service, or community resource systems.

As a Community Health Worker II, you will play a vital role in improving access to care and helping patients navigate the healthcare system. Our RN Case Managers raise the bar by providing clinical expertise and the highest quality care in the most compassionate way. The RN Case Manager is responsible for promoting patient-centered care by coordinating the plan of care for the patient stay, managing the length of stay, ensuring appropriate resource management, and developing a safe appropriate discharge plan in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team. The RN Case Manager facilitates the progression and transition of care using established criteria and in conjunction with the multidisciplinary team. The RN Case Manager will coordinate activities that promote quality outcomes and patient throughput while supporting a balance of optimal care and appropriate resource utilization.

Performs a comprehensive assessment of psychosocial, medical and discharge needs of patients/family along with an assessment of resources appropriate and available to the patient/family
Reassesses the patient’s clinical condition as indicated. Considers patient’s readmission status or risk of readmission and develops strategies to mitigate including education on appropriately accessing healthcare resources, preventative education, and community based resources.
Coordinates the plan of care and drives the discharge plan by collaborating with the multidisciplinary health care team and in particular with the patient's physician to facilitate a successful care transition
In partnership with Social Services, the RN CM is responsible for ensuring the post-acute medical needs and level of care are appropriate
The RN CM is responsible for timely referral to Social Services when risk factors for psychosocial determinants of health are identified
Involves patient, family/responsible/significant others in identifying and clarifying needs and expectations to develop mutual and realistic goals
Evaluates progression of care using evidence-based tools and approved criteria (InterQual) throughout the episode of care; escalates progression and transition of care issues through the established chain of command
Makes appropriate referrals to third party payer, disease and case management programs for recurring patients and patients with chronic disease states
Facilitates patient throughput with an ongoing focus on an effective care transition, quality and efficiency
Documents professional recommendations, discharge plan, care coordination interventions, and case management activities to effectively communicate to all members of the health care team
Align patient’s needs with available resources to ensure a safe discharge / transition
Acts as a liaison through effective and professional communications between and with physicians, patient / family, hospital staff, and outside agencies

Our Opportunity

Chewy’s mission is to be the most trusted and convenient destination for pet parents and partners everywhere. We view pets and pet parents as family and are obsessed with meeting their needs and exceeding expectations through every interaction. Within Chewy, the Payments team improves the customer and care team experience by launching better ways to pay, increasing payment success, strengthening payment reliability, and reducing the cost and operational friction of payments.

To support this mission, Chewy is hiring a Senior Program Manager, Payment Operations and Optimization
in Bellevue, WA, Boston, MA, or Plantation, FL
. This role will report to the Head of Payment Partnerships & Operations and serve as a senior operational owner for complex payment capabilities across Chewy. The role will drive payment performance, operational readiness, partner escalation, incident response, and cross-functional execution across recurring, stored payment, and advanced authorization experiences. This includes Autoship and repeat purchase payment flows, stored credentials, backup payment methods, retries, decline recovery, tokenization, digital wallets, payment method lifecycle management, and scenarios involving multiple authorizations or merchant category code (MCC) configurations.

The ideal candidate is an experienced payments and operations leader who has managed payment outcomes in a scaled ecommerce, fintech, subscription, retail, or omnichannel environment. This person brings strong payments knowledge, senior program leadership, and the ability to connect strategic priorities with hands-on operational execution across complex card-not-present and recurring payment models. They can simplify technical payment topics, identify customer and business impact, and lead cross-functional teams through measurable improvements in payment success, authorization performance, customer retention, and operational reliability. This role is well suited for someone who can partner effectively across Product, Engineering, Customer Care, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Legal/Compliance, and external payment partners to improve customer experiences.

What You'll Do

Own the operational health, performance, and optimization roadmap for advanced authorization capabilities, stored payment, and recurring, including multi-authorization flows, multiple MCC configurations, and payment method lifecycle workflows.
Define, monitor, and improve key payment metrics, including payment success rate, authorization performance, retry recovery, decline trends, multi-authorization outcomes, MCC configuration impacts, incident volume, and operational SLA performance.
Serve as the senior payment operations owner for launches, enhancements, defects, partner escalations, operational readiness, and post-launch performance management.
Lead cross-functional programs across Product, Engineering, Customer Care, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Legal/Compliance, and external payment partners.
Identify payment defects, reliability risks, and customer friction across complex authorization, stored credential, and recurring flows; quantify customer, operational, and financial impact; and drive prioritized resolution.
Partner with payment processors, wallet providers, tokenization providers, and other third parties to manage operational performance, roadmap dependencies, issue resolution, SLAs, and improvement plans.
Analyze issuer, network, processor, card type, wallet, MCC, tokenization, debit routing, retry, and decline-code trends to identify optimization opportunities.
Build executive-ready narratives, business reviews, and recommendations that connect payment performance, customer experience, retention, cost, risk, and business impact.
Serve as a payments subject matter expert for card-not-present, stored credential, recurring billing, multi-authorization, tokenization, digital wallet, debit routing, MCC, refund, reconciliation, and operational support workflows.

What You'll Need

Bachelor's degree in business, finance, operations, technology, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of experience in payments, fintech, ecommerce, retail, subscription billing, omnichannel operations, or another scaled operational environment.
5+ years leading complex cross-functional programs with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Customer Care/Operations, Legal/Compliance, and external partners.
Experience supporting complex order and payment scenarios where a single order or customer transaction may require multiple authorizations, MCC configurations, settlement paths, or downstream reconciliation.
Demonstrated experience owning payment KPIs and operational outcomes such as payment success rate, authorization rate, decline rate, retry recovery, backup payment method performance, involuntary churn, dispute rate, reconciliation quality, cost of payments, or operational SLA performance.
Direct experience with card-not-present and recurring payment flows, including processors, acquirers, issuers, card networks, digital wallets, stored credentials, tokenization, account updater, settlement, refunds, disputes, and reconciliation.
Experience supporting ecommerce, subscription, and repeat purchase payment environments where reliability directly affects customer retention and business performance.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to use payment data, processor reporting, decline trends, authorization performance, customer feedback, and operational defects to identify root causes and drive action.
Proven ability to operate in ambiguity, dive deep into details, and lead teams through issue resolution without direct authority.
Strong vendor and partner management experience, including performance reviews, escalations, SLA management, roadmap alignment, and operational improvement plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive-level narratives, business reviews, and decision recommendations.
Ability to deliver time-sensitive initiatives while maintaining strong attention to detail and ownership of follow-through.
Ability to travel up to 15% of the time.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with payment models that include multi-authorization flows, multiple MCC configurations, settlement, and reconciliation.
Experience improving authorization performance through issuer, network, processor, card type, tokenization, digital wallet, debit routing, MCC, or decline-code analysis.
Experience launching or scaling payment capabilities that support high-volume stored payment methods.
Experience improving payment observability, operational support models, and partner performance in a high-volume environment.
Experience with card-not-present payment operations, including ecommerce, fintech, subscription, or other complex digital payment workflows.

Success in This Role Looks Like

Recurring, stored payment, and advanced authorization workflows are reliable, measurable, and supported by clear operational mechanisms.
Payment success, authorization performance, and customer retention opportunities are identified quickly, quantified clearly, and improved through strong cross-functional ownership.
Payment partner performance is actively managed through business reviews, escalations, SLAs, and improvement plans.
Senior leaders have a clear view of payment performance, authorization risks, tradeoffs, and investment needs.
